stories.headline: World must move from endless war to end of war: PM Modi to Putin
stories.title: World must move from endless war to end of war: PM Modi to Putin
stories.summary: PM Modi and Russian President Putin discuss conflicts in Ukraine and the Black Sea region; PM highlights attacks on Indian mariners and reiterates that “dialogue and diplomacy” are essential to resolve conflicts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (August 31, 2026) met Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek and said the world “must move from endless war to an end of war for the benefit of humanity”.

The External Affairs Ministry said the two leaders discussed conflicts in West Asia and in the Black Sea region, where, in recent months, Indian seafarers have been attacked by both Russian and Ukrainian forces.
“Had extensive discussions with President Putin.
Discussed the full range of the India-Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership.
It is gladdening to see significant progress across various sectors in recent years.
Focus areas for India-Russia friendship remain energy, innovation, space, fertilisers, and people-to-people linkages,” said Prime Minister Modi.

In a statement, the Ministry said, “They also shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers.
The Prime Minister reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy were the way forward in resolving conflicts.”
The upcoming BRICS summit featured prominently in the discussion, and Mr. Modi said he “looks forward to welcoming President Putin in India for the 18th BRICS summit on 12-13 September”.

The Bishkek meeting between Mr. Modi and Mr. Putin featured in talks during External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s visit to the Kremlin on August 24, 2026, when Mr. Putin had indicated that he would meet Prime Minister Modi in Kyrgyzstan and also at the BRICS summit in Delhi.

“This time, our meeting is taking place on the eve of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit – an organisation that works to deepen contacts among the countries of the Global South and East, promotes the region’s socioeconomic and cultural development, and contributes to building a just multipolar world,” said President Putin in his remarks, reminding that next year will mark the 80th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between New Delhi and Moscow.
Mr. Putin noted that the number of Indian students in Russia has increased almost seven-fold in a decade, and currently 40,000 Indians are studying in Russia.

stories.headline: Bihar CM urges Union Minister of Jal Shakti to accelerate irrigation and flood control projects
stories.title: Bihar CM urges Union Minister of Jal Shakti to accelerate irrigation and flood control projects
stories.summary: Samrat Choudhary urged for the early approval and release of central assistance for pending irrigation and flood management projects announced in the Union Budget, including the Kosi-Mechi Inter-State River Link Project.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'union budget' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Monday (August 31, 2026) urged Union Minister of Jal Shakti C.R. Patil to accelerate water resource, irrigation, and flood management projects concerning Bihar.

Accompanied by Bihar Deputy Chief Minister and Water Resources Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary in Delhi, the CM informed Mr. Patil that the Union Budget 2024-25 had announced financial assistance for several schemes in the irrigation and water resources sector for Bihar, including the Kosi-Mechi Inter-State River Link Project (costing ₹11,500 crore).
He added, Bihar government had submitted Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) worth ₹16,339.18 crore to the Central Government; however, only two projects have received approval so far.

The Kosi-Mechi Inter-State River Link Project, valued at approximately ₹3,652.56 crore, will help to expand irrigation facilities in North Bihar by making better use of the surplus water from the Kosi basin.
Provisions totalling ₹965.41 crore have been made for the project’s first phase—₹395.41 crore for the 2025-26 financial year and ₹570 crore for 2026-27.
However, only ₹156.745 crore has been received so far.
Mr. Choudhary urged the early release of the remaining funds for the first phase and the approval of the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the second phase.
He also raised the issue of the early release of the funds for Sikrahana Right Embankment construction scheme, in which the central share is ₹125.08 crore.

The status of other schemes proposed under the Union Budget 2024-25 was reviewed which includes three irrigation projects with an estimated cost of ₹5,951.45 crore and 15 flood management projects with an estimated cost of ₹3,896.14 crore, all of which are currently under consideration at various levels within the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
Progress on the Extension, Renovation, and Modernisation (ERM) of the Western Kosi Canal Project—announced in the Union Budget 2025-26—was also reviewed.
The Bihar government has submitted a DPR worth ₹8,338.89 crore for this project to the Central Water Commission (CWC).
Anticipating central assistance, the state government has already commenced work on the first phase, costing ₹3,484.24 crore, using its own resources.

stories.headline: 'No jurisdiction': India rejects Permanent Court of Arbitration's order on suspension of Indus Waters Treaty
stories.title: 'No jurisdiction': India rejects Permanent Court of Arbitration's order on suspension of Indus Waters Treaty
stories.summary: New Delhi, Aug 31: India on Monday rejected the Permanent Court of Arbitration's order setting aside its decision to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan, saying the "illegally-constituted" body has no jurisdiction to comment on New Delhi's sovereign decisions. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance remains in force. New Delhi decided to put the IWT in abeyance as part of a series of punitive diplomatic and economic measures unveiled soon after the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year that killed 26 civilians. Pakistan had approached the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague in March this year to determine the status of the treaty virtually challenging India's action. "Today, the illegally constituted so-called Court of Arbitration (CoA) has issued what it termed as an award concerning Interim Measures and Status of the Indus Waters Treaty," the MEA said. "This so called Court was constituted by the World Bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty and India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body," it added. India has never recognised the "existence in law of this illegally-constituted and so-called Court of Arbitration", and has always said the "very establishment of this alleged arbitral body constitutes a grave violation of the Indus Waters Treaty", the MEA said in a statement. "Accordingly, India has never appeared before this body and has refused to take any cognisance of its earlier pronouncements," it said. The MEA said the Court of Arbitration has "no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India's sovereign decisions." "Its pronouncements, now or in the future, will have no effect on India's actions in connection with the projects being undertaken by India," it said. In the last few months, India has stepped up work on several hydropower projects in Jammu and Kashmir that Pakistan had opposed under the provisions of the pact signed in 1960. The Permanent Court of Arbitration said the court considered the meaning of India's decision to suspend the treaty, "finding that it could only be a claim that the Indus Waters Treaty is either suspended or terminated". The court examined the potential grounds on which India can suspend or terminate the Treaty, including grounds cited by New Delhi in its public statements. "In a unanimous decision, the Court found that none of these grounds could justify suspension or termination of the Treaty. Accordingly, the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the Treaty, including those relating to the design and operation of its hydro-electric projects on the Western Rivers," the Permanent Court of Arbitration said in a media statement. New Delhi has been maintaining that IWT will continue to be held in abeyance until Pakistan "credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism". The court said that while India did not participate by making written or oral submissions during proceedings, it took into account India's positions on the issues to the extent "they could be discerned from India's statements and conduct outside of these proceedings (including Indian government communications to Pakistan and to the neutral expert, and public statements made by Indian officials)". The court noted that it looked "extremely seriously" into India's allegation that "Pakistan's sponsorship of cross-border terrorism had impeded its utilisation of rights" under the Indus Waters Treaty. "However, the Court found that even if India's allegation was assumed to be true, they would not establish a material breach of the Treaty by Pakistan," the court said. It said the treaty "does not address terrorism or the use of force and expressly indicates that it governs only the rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the use of the waters of the Indus Rivers System".

stories.headline: Launched after Pahalgam attack, J&K CM's helpline now a lifeline for many
stories.title: Launched after Pahalgam attack, J&K CM's helpline now a lifeline for many
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 31: What began as an emergency response to a moment of fear and uncertainty has evolved into a critical support system for Jammu and Kashmir residents across the country and beyond. The dedicated toll-free helpline (1800-8900-166), launched by the Omar Abdullah-led government on April 25, 2025, has emerged as a round-the-clock bridge between the administration and people in need, handling everything from distress calls and emergency assistance to grievance redressal and coordination with authorities in other states. The helpline was set up in the immediate aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack, when reports of intimidation, harassment and assaults on students and residents of Jammu and Kashmir studying or working outside the Union Territory began to surface. Faced with growing anxiety among families, the Chief Minister's Office moved swiftly to establish a 24x7 control mechanism to provide immediate assistance, ensure coordination with state governments and law-enforcement agencies, and offer a direct channel for citizens seeking help. Officials said that the service has since grown far beyond its original mandate, transforming into a single-window support platform for Kashmiris facing difficulties across India and abroad. The helpline has been used to assist students, facilitate emergency travel, coordinate with local administrations, and address a range of public-service related issues. One of its most notable interventions came during the Iran-Israel conflict, when scores of students from Jammu and Kashmir found themselves stranded amid escalating tensions. The helpline played a key role in maintaining communication with affected students, coordinating with their families back home, and facilitating the flow of information between the administration and those caught in the crisis. The service also earned widespread appreciation in the aftermath of the Pahalgam attack, with students and families describing it as a dependable point of contact during a period of uncertainty and fear. Remarkably, the operation is being managed by a single officer posted at the Chief Minister's Secretariat, who monitors calls, coordinates responses and follows up with departments and authorities across jurisdictions. Despite its lean structure, officials say the helpline has responded to thousands of calls and messages, often serving as the first point of contact for people seeking urgent intervention. Government sources said the initiative reflects the administration's effort to remain accessible beyond traditional office channels and ensure that residents of Jammu and Kashmir, irrespective of where they are located, have a direct line to the government. As the helpline completes more than a year of operations, it has increasingly come to be viewed not merely as an emergency contact number, but as a reassurance mechanism for students, workers, professionals and families from Jammu and Kashmir navigating challenges far from home. For many, a call to 1800-8900-166 has become synonymous with the assurance that help is only a phone call away.

stories.headline: India's GDP grows 7.8 percent in Q1FY27, up from 6.9 percent a year ago
stories.title: India's GDP grows 7.8 percent in Q1FY27, up from 6.9 percent a year ago
stories.summary: India’s economy grew 7.8 percent in the April-June quarter of 2026-27, a sharp pick-up from the 6.9 percent pace recorded in the same period last year and a signal that domestic demand and investment activity are gathering momentum, according to government data released on Monday. The Q1FY27 figures were, however, lower than the 8.6 percent growth seen in Q4FY26.Real gross domestic product (GDP) touched Rs 81.36 lakh crore in Q1FY27, up from Rs 75.46 lakh crore a year earlier. In nominal terms, with GDP not adjusted for inflation, GDP rose 10.3 percent to Rs 88.27 lakh crore, against Rs 80 lakh crore in Q1FY26. Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, says that this growth in nominal figures was aided by higher inflation, which enters the deflation indices.“Overall, economic activity remained robust during the April-June quarter despite the adverse impact of the West Asia conflict on some sectors as well as the unfolding impact of the uneven monsoon,” says Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA.Meanwhile, gross value added (GVA) expanded 8.2 percent in real terms and 11.5 percent in nominal terms in the same quarter. “The higher growth in GVA relative to GDP can be accounted for by the higher subsidy bill which is netted from taxes. This was due to higher food and fertiliser subsidy bills,” says Sabnavis.Also Read: India's Industrial Output Slows to 6.7% in July as Mining ContractsThe tertiary sector was the biggest driver of growth, expanding 10 percent at constant prices, with the Financial, Real Estate, IT and Professional Services segment growing 12.1 percent.The secondary sector, comprising manufacturing, utilities and construction, grew 8.6 percent, led by a 9.2 percent rise in manufacturing, compared to 8.3 percent in Q1FY26. “Here it is again the infra based companies which have contributed to growth based on the results of companies for Q1,” says Sabnavis, adding that the growth in manufacturing in this quarter has been “very impressive.” Nayar believes the manufacturing numbers likely reflect the uptick in volume growth between these quarters, amid an unfavourable base. In addition, the construction segment grew 7.7 percent.However, the primary sector lagged, growing just 2.9 percent, as agriculture expanded 3.6 percent, lower than the 4.4 percent growth in the same quarter last year, while mining and quarrying contracted 2.4 percent. On the lower growth print in agriculture, Sabnavis says, “One cannot read much into this number as this is residual rabi and more of allied activities which were affected by floods.”On the expenditure side, Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF), a key gauge of investment activity, surged 11.9 percent at constant prices, more than double the 5.8 percent growth seen in Q1FY26, pointing to stronger capital spending by companies and the government. Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) rose 7.1 percent, while government consumption spending grew a more modest 4.3 percent. Exports grew 12 percent even as imports contracted 1.1 percent.

stories.headline: After Supreme Court refusal to halt CJP march, Delhi Police seeks quashing of FIRs against NEET-UG protesters, students
stories.title: After Supreme Court refusal to halt CJP march, Delhi Police seeks quashing of FIRs against NEET-UG protesters, students
stories.summary: Supreme Court agrees to hear Centre’s application on September 1; the court expects both sides, those who wish to march, and the police, to respect and honour the laws of the land, Chief Justice Surya Kant says
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: Within hours of the Supreme Court refusing on Monday (August 31, 2026) to halt a protest march announced by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in central Delhi ahead of the BRICS Summit, the Delhi.
Police moved an urgent plea to quash First Information Reports (FIRs) registered against students and youths who participated in the NEET-UG paper leak protests.

Days before the BRICS Summit on September 12-13, the CJP decided to hit the streets again on September 5, citing the Centre’s failure to live up to its assurances, including the immediate withdrawal of FIRs against student protesters.
Earlier in the day, a three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant found no “compelling circumstance” to interfere with CJP’s plans for a protest march.
In the afternoon, as the Bench was preparing to rise for the day, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta orally mentioned an application filed by the Delhi.
Police urging the apex court to invoke Article 142 of the Constitution to quash the FIRs.
Mr. Mehta pushed for a hearing on September 1 itself.

The Delhi Police said it “no longer wished” to pursue the FIRs registered across various police stations in central Delhi, from Barakhamba Road to Parliament Street to Connaught Place, against students and protesters following the crackdown on July 20.
These FIRs had arraigned charges of rioting, attempt to murder, and damage to public property against protesters.
The police expressed willingness to close any other FIRs which were not mentioned in the application.
They sought the court’s permission to file a “fresh, specific” FIRs only against 2,873 individuals with criminal antecedents, who were reported to be present at the NEET-UG protest site.
Chief Justice Kant agreed to list the application on September 1, remarking, “If parties are reconciling, we have no difficulties.”

stories.headline: India looks for 'sustainable way' to stay in Chabahar amid US sanctions
stories.title: India looks for 'sustainable way' to stay in Chabahar amid US sanctions
stories.summary: India looks for 'sustainable way' to stay in Chabahar amid US sanctions
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The statement is significant as it comes amid uncertainty over India's future at Chabahar following the expiry of a US sanctions waiver.
It also comes amid reports that New Delhi is considering temporarily transferring its stake in the project to an Iranian entity to reduce its exposure to US sanctions.

India is looking for a “sustainable way forward” to continue its involvement in Iran's Chabahar port amid US sanctions, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said, as New Delhi weighs options to protect its stake in the strategic project.

“We have been associated with this project over a long period of time,” Misri said in Bishkek, noting that the conflict in West Asia had affected regional cooperation and the “regime” under which activities at Chabahar could be carried out.
“We remain in discussion and in touch with various stakeholders in order to find a sustainable way forward to continue this element of cooperation,” he said.

Misri's remarks come after the expiry of a US sanctions waiver and amid reports that India could temporarily transfer its stake in the project to an Iranian entity to reduce its exposure to US penalties.
According to a Bloomberg report, India is discussing options separately with the US and Iran over its $120 million investment in the port.
One option is to temporarily transfer India's stake to an Iranian entity during the sanctions period.
India, however, does not plan to completely exit Chabahar, the report said.
Such an arrangement could allow New Delhi to step back from direct operations for now while keeping open the possibility of returning if sanctions are eased.
Misri's emphasis on finding a way to “continue” cooperation is therefore important.
It indicates that India is looking at ways to preserve its involvement in Chabahar even if the present arrangement has to change.

stories.headline: Supreme Court seeks government response on plea to ban retail sale of acid
stories.title: Supreme Court seeks government response on plea to ban retail sale of acid
stories.summary: Petitioners have raised concerns over the use of corrosive substance in crimes against women
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (August 31, 2026) sought the Union government’s response to a plea for a ban on retail sale of acid after concerns were raised over the use of the corrosive substance in crimes against women.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, the petitioners, represented by senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal, and acid-attack survivor activist Shaheen Malik, said acid was still available in outlets for the asking despite the apex court’s 2013 directions regulating its retail sale.
In the alternative to a complete ban, the court was urged to direct the Centre to frame a scheme to ensure strict regulation of the retail sale of acid in the market.

“We are informed that certain guidelines were laid down in 2013, which have more or less become obsolete and are not being followed… The Union government shall also respond as to why a complete ban on the retail sale of acid should not be imposed, or, in the alternative, whether such sale should be permitted subject to stringent regulatory measures,” the court recorded in the order.
The Bench further directed the Centre, States and Union Territories to formulate appropriate rehabilitation and compensation measures for victims of acid attacks within six weeks.
It also asked the Union government to consider framing a model scheme and providing necessary assistance to States for its effective implementation.
The Bench further asked the States and the Union Territories to furnish an update on the number of acid attack cases, chargesheets filed and the pendency of these cases.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, had said on July 14 that the government made changes in the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, to extend the benefits of the law to those acid attack victims who suffer internal injuries due to forced ingestion.

stories.headline: Muscat Authorities Examining Claims Of Ransom Calls To Family Of Indian Captain Missing After Hormuz Attack : Centre Tells Supreme Court
stories.title: Muscat Authorities Examining Claims Of Ransom Calls To Family Of Indian Captain Missing After Hormuz Attack : Centre Tells Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union government today told the Supreme Court that the Muscat authorities are examining the claims of ransom calls received by the family of merchant navy captain Ashish Kumar, who was feared dead after a drone/missile attack in the Strait of Hormuz.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was informed by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta that DNA profiling of the mortal remains, believed to be of captain Kumar's and found on the merchant vessel, could not be done by Muscat authorities, as the remains were severely burnt.

On the claims of the merchant navy captain's family that there had been ransom calls since his disappearance and there was a possibility of him being alive as the DNA matching was not successful, the SG said that the Muscat authorities were looking into the matter.
"The bones which were recovered were so burnt that it could not be analyzed by DNA.
There was one more concern the family has raised - that the mobile phone of the captain was found and that was sometimes showing holding...
DP (display picture) was also changed.
Our Embassy in Muscat has reported this fact to their counterpart", the SG said.
The captain's wife claimed to have received multiple ransom calls in March, which raised a demand of Rs.2 million.

The SG said that in view of the suspicious ransom calls and negative DNA report, the family had requested intensive efforts for searching the captain, tracking of the mobile phones, and investigation of the related records.
He stated that a letter was received from the Muscat authorities that they are examining the matter and doing what they can.
The CJI told the petitioner's counsel to take a copy of the report from the SG and posted the matter on Monday.

stories.headline: Amid Lawyers' Protest, Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice SP Sharma Goes On Leave
stories.title: Amid Lawyers' Protest, Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice SP Sharma Goes On Leave
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma has gone on leave for three days amid protests by members of the Bar against his continuation as Acting Chief Justice.
As per the updated roster for Jaipur bench, the Acting CJ will not be holding any sitting from September 1 to September 5.

The development comes against the backdrop of protests by lawyers, who have been demanding that Justice Sharma be relieved of the charge of Acting Chief Justice and that a permanent Chief Justice be appointed to the Rajasthan High Court.

The protest followed recent letters sent by Justice Sandeep Mehta of the Supreme Court to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant raising grave complaints against ACJ Sharma regarding maladministration and favouritism.
Justice Mehta also urged the CJI to appoint a Chief Justice from another High Court.

Following the decision of the Rajasthan High Court bar to abstain from work till September 6, the Rajasthan High Court Advocate Clerks Association, Jodhpur has also announced its decision to abstain from work at the Jodhpur Bench.
Justice Shamra is set to retire on September 26.
